summary: Sibani Dasgupta was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Dhaka and under Rajendra Chandra Hazra. She completed her doctorate at the University of Calcutta by 1954 under the supervision of Sushil Kumar De.

Sibnath Sarma worked in philosophy and Indology. He served at the Research and Archaeological Department in Jammu and Kashmir, and was an attested professor in Gauhati University's Department of Philosophy between 1999 and 2012.

Sibraj Chetry is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sibnath Sarma, D. K. Chakravarty, N. Sharma, Girish Sarma, and M. Boruah, and was attested as a lecturer of philosophy at North Lakhimpur College in 2012.

Sicheng Liang (1901–1972) was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at Beijing Huiwen Middle School, Tsinghua University (~1915–1923), and the University of Pennsylvania School of Design (~1924–1927), later holding a post at Peking University.

Siegfried Goldschmidt (1844–1884) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Berlin, Leipzig, Göttingen, and Tübingen (Ph.D. 1867), studying under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. In 1881, he became assistant professor at the University of Strasbourg.

Siegfried Lienhard (1924–2011) was an Indologist. He earned a Dr. phil. from Vienna (1949), studied in Paris, and habilitated at Stockholm. His posts included Kiel University (professor 1962–1968) and the University of Stockholm (professor 1968–1990).

Siglinde Dietz is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Bonn in 1980 under Michael Hahn and was affiliated with the University of Göttingen in 1990.
Signe Cohen is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied under Ludo Rocher. She holds a post as Professor at the University of Missouri.

Signe Howell (1942–2025) was a scholar in religious studies and other fields. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1970–1973) and the University of Oxford (~1974–1980), and was appointed professor at the University of Oslo in 1989.

Silvio Vita (1954–2023) studied at Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology. He held posts at "L'Orientale", Naples Federico II, Rome, and Kyoto University of Foreign Studies, and directed the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~2002–2013).

Simo Parpola (born 1943) is a linguistics and Assyriology scholar. After studying at the Pontifical Biblical Institute, the British Museum, and the University of Helsinki (PhD 1968), he taught at Chicago and held docent and professorial posts at Helsinki from 1973.
Simon Cubelic is an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. In 2018, he was attested at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities and served on the editorial board of Documenta Nepalica.

Simon P. James is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. At Durham University, he was attested as a tutor in the Department of Philosophy in 2001 and as a lecturer in philosophy from 2013 to 2014.
Singhathon Narāsabho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Visva-Bharati University under the supervision of Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti.

Siniruddha Dash (born 1955) works in Indology and linguistics. He served as Director at the University of Madras (2000–2014), the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library (attested 2013), and the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation.

Siran Upendra Deraniyagala (1942–2021) was an archaeologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, the University of London under Raymond Allchin, and Harvard University. He served as Director General of the Department of Archaeology, Sri Lanka, from around 1992 to 2001.

Sisir Roy is a scholar in philosophy and other fields who studied under Debabrata Sensharma. In 2009, he was attested as a professor at the Indian Statistical Institute and held a post at the National Institute of Advanced Studies.
Sister Vajirā (1928–1991) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Paul Debes and, in 1955, under traditional teacher Narada Maha Thera.
Sita Krishna Nambiar is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Bonn under the doctoral supervision of Paul Hacker.

Sita Ram Roy studied history, archaeology, and Indology under doctoral supervisors Anant Sadashiv Altekar and Ram Sharan Sharma. He was a Fellow at K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute, Gaya Museum curator, and Bihar Directorate officer in 1971.
